lines.text: Somewhere, a cardboard delivery box is about to become papier-mâché.
A patio reservation is about to become an indoor table with a worse view.
I hope your umbrella matches your outfit. Something ought to.
They make rain covers for everything now. Still nothing for your opinions.
Snowblower owners are about to become the least humble people in the neighborhood.
Even the garbage cans will look photogenic. Nature's standards are slipping.
Snow makes almost everything look charming. I won't make promises about you.
Fashion magazines call it layering. Everyone else calls it getting dressed.
Somebody will spend longer arguing against another layer than putting one on.
I can recommend another layer. Making it look intentional on you is harder.
Someone will refuse to take a layer off out of sheer principle.
Somebody will spend the warm-up arguing that it still isn't warm enough.
I can remove a layer from the drawing. The attitude is welded on.
Wet umbrellas are just portable puddles once they've done their job.
If only you folded up as neatly as the umbrella.
The 'capsule wardrobe' crowd will be unbearable about this.
The clothing industry will somehow find a way to charge extra for this simplicity.
This forecast is the closest you'll get to having a signature look.
That's a lot of trust to put in your taste.
